_comment: The published rubric for E7's assessment. Turn 10g lists 'rubric written and
published' as the first gate before certification can go live on a module,
and published means a learner can read it BEFORE sitting — not that it exists
in a database somewhere. A learner who cannot see how they will be judged is
being examined, not taught, and this project is not an examination board.
Structure comes from 10f: one written answer, four criteria, each banded
individually. 'Three or four secure gives secure; two gives nearly.' A note is
required on any criterion below secure — record_review() refuses without one,
because actionable feedback is the entire value of a human read.
The criteria themselves are NOT the design's. 10f illustrates the rubric with
'weighs both options' and 'uses a number to argue', which belong to the
everyday-money module its mock shows. Lrnon's E7 is Truth, Verification &
Critical Thinking, so the criteria are drawn from what that module actually
teaches: triage (L2), primary sources (L3, L4), and stating uncertainty (L8).
The fourth is kept verbatim because it is module-independent.

task.prompt: A colleague forwards you a striking statistic about your field and wants to put it in tomorrow's presentation. Explain, in your own words, how you would decide whether to rely on it.
task.guidance: What the reviewer looks for is how you reason, not whether you reach our answer. Own words matter more than neat words.

criteria.name: Decides whether it is worth checking
criteria.secure: Asks what turns on the claim before reaching for a source. Says plainly that some claims do not need checking.
criteria.nearly: Checks everything, or checks nothing, without saying why this one.
criteria.not_yet: Treats verification as a reflex with no sense of what is at stake.

criteria.name: Goes to the primary source
criteria.secure: Names the original publication and says they would open it and read the sentence in place — not a restatement of it.
criteria.nearly: Says they would 'search for it' or 'check online' without distinguishing a source from a report of one.
criteria.not_yet: Would ask a model whether the claim is true, or accept a second article repeating it.

criteria.name: Names a risk or trade-off
criteria.secure: Identifies something that could still be wrong after checking — a definition that differs, a date, a population the figure does not cover.
criteria.nearly: Acknowledges uncertainty in general terms without locating it anywhere specific.
criteria.not_yet: Treats a verified figure as settled.

criteria.name: Own words, own reasoning
criteria.secure: Reads as a person thinking. States what they checked and what they did not, which is the module's closing formula.
criteria.nearly: Recites the module's three questions without applying them to this case.
criteria.not_yet: Reproduces lesson text, or reads as generated.

banding.rule: Three or four criteria at secure gives secure. Exactly two gives nearly. Fewer gives not yet.
banding.noteRequired: Any criterion below secure needs a written note the learner can act on.
banding.nameHidden: The reviewer does not see who wrote the answer. The name is attached after the decision, never before.

ifNoReviewer: If no reviewer is free, the auto-marked sections band the attempt on score and the certificate issues immediately at that band. A reviewer reads the written answer later and can only raise it. Nothing is taken away by an upgrade.
